# EnterpriseGlue v0.27.4 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.27.3`.

## Highlights

- **database:** Lets the least-privilege PostgreSQL schema-epoch preflight verify existing tables and RLS policies without business-data access.

## User and administrator impact

- Pooled PostgreSQL upgrades no longer reject a ready schema because the dedicated preflight login cannot see protected tables through information_schema.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Deploy the matching backend image and host chart through the normal migration and schema-epoch preflight sequence.

## Configuration

- No configuration or additional PostgreSQL grants are required; the preflight login retains SELECT only on the migration ledger and no business-table access.

## Database migrations

- No schema, policy, role, or grant is changed; verification reads PostgreSQL system catalogs and the signed migration ledger only.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- The membership-free preflight login retains zero business-table privileges while verifying relation presence and exact RLS policy catalogs.
- Generic bootstrap and data-integrity reads remain on application and owner invocations and are excluded from the dedicated schema-epoch preflight.

## Rollback

- Redeploy the preceding backend image and chart; no database rollback or credential change is required.

## Validation evidence

- Unit tests preserve migration orchestration and verify that the schema-epoch preflight skips business-table inspection.
- A PostgreSQL 16 integration test proves the preflight login has no business-table SELECT or DML privileges and no information_schema visibility while catalog-backed relation and RLS verification succeeds.
